    def test_multilinecontinuationerror_attributes(self):
        # MultilineContinuationError carries source, lineno, line
        # and is a subclass of ParsingError.
        import pickle
        e1 = configparser.MultilineContinuationError('src', 42, '  x\n')
        self.assertIsInstance(e1, configparser.ParsingError)
        self.assertEqual(e1.source, 'src')
        self.assertEqual(e1.lineno, 42)
        self.assertEqual(e1.line, '  x\n')
        self.assertEqual(e1.args, ('src', 42, '  x\n'))
        for proto in range(pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL + 1):
            pickled = pickle.dumps(e1, proto)
            e2 = pickle.loads(pickled)
            self.assertEqual(e1.message, e2.message)
            self.assertEqual(e1.args, e2.args)
            self.assertEqual(e1.source, e2.source)
            self.assertEqual(e1.lineno, e2.lineno)
            self.assertEqual(e1.line, e2.line)
            self.assertEqual(repr(e1), repr(e2))

    def test_multilinecontinuationerror_read_string(self):
        # ConfigParser.read_string raises MultilineContinuationError
        # when a valueless option is followed by an indented line.
        parser = configparser.ConfigParser(allow_no_value=True)
        with self.assertRaises(
                configparser.MultilineContinuationError) as cm:
            parser.read_string("[section]\nkey\n  continuation\n")
        exc = cm.exception
        self.assertEqual(exc.source, '<string>')
        self.assertEqual(exc.lineno, 3)
        self.assertEqual(exc.line, '  continuation\n')

    def test_multilinecontinuationerror_read_file(self):
        # RawConfigParser.read_file raises the same exception.
        import tempfile
        parser = configparser.RawConfigParser(allow_no_value=True)
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', suffix='.ini',
                                          delete=False) as f:
            f.write("[section]\nkey\n  continuation\n")
            fname = f.name
        try:
            with self.assertRaises(
                    configparser.MultilineContinuationError) as cm:
                with open(fname, 'r') as fp:
                    parser.read_file(fp)
            exc = cm.exception
            self.assertEqual(exc.source, fname)
            self.assertEqual(exc.lineno, 3)
            self.assertEqual(exc.line, '  continuation\n')
            self.assertIsInstance(exc, configparser.ParsingError)
        finally:
            os.unlink(fname)

    def test_multilinecontinuationerror_valid_multiline(self):
        # A valued multiline option is still parsed correctly.
        parser = configparser.ConfigParser(allow_no_value=True)
        parser.read_string("[section]\nkey = value\n  more\n")
        self.assertTrue(parser.has_option('section', 'key'))

    def test_multilinecontinuationerror_valueless_no_continuation(self):
        # A valueless option without an indented continuation is fine.
        parser = configparser.ConfigParser(allow_no_value=True)
        parser.read_string("[section]\nkey\nother = val\n")
        self.assertTrue(parser.has_option('section', 'key'))

.. exception:: MultilineContinuationError

   Raised when an indented continuation line follows a valueless option
   (an option with no value, as permitted by ``allow_no_value=True``).
   This is a subclass of :exc:`!ParsingError`.

   The constructor takes three arguments: ``source`` (the name of the
   source being parsed, or ``'<string>'`` for string input), ``lineno``
   (the one-based line number of the offending continuation line), and
   ``line`` (the exact text of that line, including its trailing
   newline).  All three values are stored as attributes of the same
   name and are preserved in ``args`` for pickling and copying.

   .. attribute:: source

   .. attribute:: lineno

   .. attribute:: line

   .. versionadded:: 3.12

.. rubric:: Footnotes
